title: Practice: compound units
intro: Write times as decimals of an hour, and convert the top and bottom units separately.

questions.prompt: Match each unit to what it measures.
questions.explanation: Read the unit as a division: distance ÷ time, mass ÷ volume, force ÷ area, volume ÷ time.

questions.prompt: A car travels $174$ km in $2$ hours $24$ minutes. Find its average speed in km/h.
A plane flies at $840$ km/h for $2$ hours $45$ minutes. How far does it travel?
How many **minutes** does it take to walk $3.5$ km at $5$ km/h?
A block of wood measures $20$ cm by $10$ cm by $5$ cm and has mass $650$ g. Find its density in $\text{g/cm}^3$.
questions.explanation: $V = 1000\ \text{cm}^3$, so density $= 650 \div 1000 = 0.65\ \text{g/cm}^3$. It floats — less dense than water.

questions.prompt: Steel has density $7800\ \text{kg/m}^3$. Find the mass, in kg, of a steel rod of volume $1500\ \text{cm}^3$.
hints: Change the volume to $\text{m}^3$: divide by $1\,000\,000$.

questions.prompt: A force of $450$ N acts on an area of $1500\ \text{cm}^2$. Find the pressure in $\text{N/m}^2$.
Average speed for a journey in stages.
questions.scenario: Tan drives $45$ km at $60$ km/h, stops for $20$ minutes, then drives $105$ km at $90$ km/h.

steps.prompt: Time for the first stage, in minutes.
Time for the second stage, in minutes.
Total time for the whole journey, in hours.
Average speed for the whole journey.

questions.explanation: Total distance $150$ km; total time $2.25$ h including the stop. $150 \div 2.25 = 66.7$ km/h.

questions.prompt: A tap fills a $0.24\ \text{m}^3$ tank at $8$ litres per minute. How long does it take, in minutes?
Two metals are melted together: $300\ \text{cm}^3$ of copper (density $8.9\ \text{g/cm}^3$) and $200\ \text{cm}^3$ of zinc (density $7.1\ \text{g/cm}^3$). Find the density of the mixture.
hints: Find the mass of each metal.
questions.explanation: Copper: $300 \times 8.9 = 2670$ g. Zinc: $200 \times 7.1 = 1420$ g. Total $4090$ g in $500\ \text{cm}^3$: $4090 \div 500 = 8.18\ \text{g/cm}^3$. Averaging the densities (8.0) is wrong — there is more copper.
